draft.title: The standard model
card: The standard model describes the smallest known building blocks of matter and the forces between them. Matter is made of quarks and leptons.
Quarks
particles that join in groups to make larger particles. Protons and neutrons are each made of three quarks. Up and down quarks make up ordinary protons and neutrons.
Leptons
particles that are not made of quarks. The electron is a lepton. The neutrino is another lepton.
Force carriers
forces act through exchange particles. The photon carries the electromagnetic force. Gluons carry the strong force, which holds quarks together inside protons and neutrons.
draft.remember: Quarks and leptons make matter. Exchange particles such as photons and gluons carry the forces.

a.q: Which statement about a proton is correct, according to the standard model?
opts: It is made of three quarks
It is a lepton like the electron
It is a force carrier like the photon
It is a single particle with no parts
a.why: A proton is made of three quarks held together by gluons. It is not a lepton, because leptons are not made of quarks. It is not a force carrier, because those are exchange particles.
a.clue: Think about what protons and neutrons are made of.

b.q: A student says that an electron is made of quarks held together by gluons. Which reply is correct?
opts: No, an electron is a lepton and not made of quarks
No, an electron is a force carrier like the photon
Yes, all matter particles are made of quarks
Yes, but it has only two quarks, unlike a proton
b.why: The electron is a lepton, and leptons are not made of quarks. Only particles such as protons and neutrons are built from quarks. The idea that all matter is quarks is tempting, but matter is made of quarks and leptons.
b.clue: Matter has two families of building blocks. Which one includes the electron?

a.best: It is made of three quarks

b.best: No, an electron is a lepton and not made of quarks

problems.detail: Leptons are defined only as 'particles that are not made of quarks'. That definition also fits photons, gluons and other force carriers, and even quarks themselves, none of which are leptons. Leptons should be described as fundamental matter particles, like the electron and neutrino, that are not made of quarks and do not feel the strong force.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear correct answer and the explanations match. The card's definition of a lepton as any particle not made of quarks is wrong, because it would also include photons, gluons and quarks, so it should be tightened.

proposal.title: The standard model
card: The standard model describes the fundamental particles of matter and the forces between them. Fundamental means they have no known smaller parts. Matter is made of quarks and leptons.
Quarks
fundamental matter particles that feel the strong force and join in groups to make larger particles. Protons and neutrons are each made of three quarks, a mix of up and down quarks.
Leptons
fundamental matter particles that are not made of quarks and do not feel the strong force. The electron and the neutrino are leptons.
Force carriers

forces act through exchange particles, which are not matter particles. The photon carries the electromagnetic force. Gluons carry the strong force, which holds quarks together inside protons and neutrons.
proposal.remember: Quarks and leptons make up matter. Exchange particles such as photons and gluons carry the forces.

a.q: Which statement about a proton is correct, according to the standard model?
opts: It is made of three quarks
It is a lepton like the electron
It is a force carrier like the photon
It is a single particle with no parts
a.why: A proton is made of three up and down quarks, held together by gluons. It cannot be a lepton, because leptons are fundamental and not made of quarks. It is a matter particle, not an exchange particle like the photon.
a.clue: Think about what protons and neutrons are built from.

b.q: A student says that an electron is made of quarks held together by gluons. Which reply is correct?
opts: No, an electron is a lepton and not made of quarks
No, an electron is a force carrier like the photon
Yes, all matter particles are made of quarks
Yes, but it has only two quarks, unlike a proton
b.why: The electron is a lepton: a fundamental matter particle with no quarks inside it. The idea that all matter is made of quarks is tempting, but matter is made of two families, quarks and leptons. The electron is not a force carrier either, as it is a matter particle.
